facts.statement: Typothorax was an extinct aetosaur that lived during the Late Triassic period.
facts.quote: Typothorax is an extinct genus of typothoracine aetosaur that lived in the Late Triassic.

facts.statement: Fossils of Typothorax have been discovered in North America.
facts.quote: Its remains have been found in North America.

facts.statement: Typothorax lived between 216 and 203 million years ago during the Late Triassic.
facts.quote: Temporal range: Late Triassic, 216–203 Ma

facts.statement: Unlike modern crocodilians, aetosaurs including Typothorax were herbivores.
facts.quote: Unlike modern crocodilians, aetosaurs were herbivorous.

facts.statement: Typothorax had small, leaf-shaped teeth that were not adapted for eating meat.
facts.quote: Typothorax and other aetosaurs possess small, leaf-shaped teeth that were unsuited for a diet consisting of meat.

facts.statement: Typothorax had lateral scutes with posteriorly hooked horns along its back and ornamented scutes covering its sides and underbelly.
facts.quote: It has lateral scutes that bear horns that are posteriorly hooked along its back, while its sides and underbelly are covered with ornamented scutes.

facts.statement: Typothorax is unique among aetosaurs for having spiked osteoderms on the underside of its tail near the cloaca.
facts.quote: Typothorax possesses spiked osteoderms on the underside of the tail, near the cloaca.

facts.statement: Typothorax had erect hindlimbs held directly beneath its body.
facts.quote: Typothorax had erect hindlimbs held beneath the body.

facts.statement: Typothorax was likely a slow-moving animal because its femur was almost equal in length to its lower leg bones.
facts.quote: Because the length of the femur is almost equal to that of the tibia and fibula (lower leg) and astragalus and calcaneum (ankle), Typothorax was probably slow-moving.

facts.statement: Several features of Typothorax's forelimbs have been interpreted as adaptations for digging.
facts.quote: Several aspects of the forelimbs have been interpreted as adaptations to digging.

facts.statement: Researchers concluded that while Typothorax was not specifically adapted for a fully burrowing lifestyle, it possessed a digging ability not found in other aetosaurs.
facts.quote: Heckert et al. (2010) concluded that Typothorax was not specifically adapted for a fossorial lifestyle but had an ability to dig that other aetosaurs didn't have.

facts.statement: Typothorax fossils have been found in the Chinle Formation of Arizona and the Bull Canyon Formation of New Mexico and Texas.
facts.quote: It has been found in Arizona, in the Chinle Formation, as well as in New Mexico and Texas in the Bull Canyon Formation of the Dockum Group.

facts.statement: Typothorax belongs to the clade Typothoracinae within the subfamily Aetosaurinae.
facts.quote: Typothorax belongs to a clade of aetosaurs called the Typothoracinae, within the subfamily Aetosaurinae.

facts.statement: A 2013 redescription found the holotype of T. coccinarum to be too fragmentary to be diagnostic, classifying it as a nomen dubium.
facts.quote: Parker (2013) redescribed the holotype of the type species of Typothorax, T. coccinarum. It was found to be too fragmentary to be diagnosable and therefore represents a nomen dubium.

facts.statement: Episcoposaurus horridus is considered the next available name for material previously referred to T. coccinarum.
facts.quote: Episcoposaurus horridus, the type species of its genus usually considered to be a junior synonym of T. coccinarum, is the next available name for material referred to T. coccinarum.

facts.statement: To preserve taxonomic stability, researchers suggested petitioning for a neotype for T. coccinarum from well-preserved specimens.
facts.quote: Nevertheless, to preserve taxonomic stability Parker (2013) suggested to attempt to petition for a neotype for T. coccinarum from well preserved specimens which have been previously referred to it.

facts.statement: Unlike some aetosaurs such as Desmatosuchus, Typothorax lacks large shoulder spikes.
facts.quote: Unlike some aetosaurs such as Desmatosuchus, Typothorax does not have large shoulder spikes.

facts.statement: Typothorax had a shortened vertebral column with individual vertebrae reduced in length.
facts.quote: The vertebral column of Typothorax is shortened, with individual vertebrae being reduced in length.

facts.statement: T. coccinarum possessed around 20 rows of presacral osteoderms and approximately 26 presacral vertebrae.
facts.quote: T. coccinarum has around 20 rows of presacral osteoderms and about 26 presacral vertebrae.

facts.statement: Two species of Typothorax are known: T. coccinarum and T. antiquum.
facts.quote: Two species are known: T. coccinarum, the type species, and T. antiquum.

facts.statement: Typothorax was an aetosaur, a pseudosuchian distant relative of modern crocodiles.
facts.quote: El typothorax era un aetosaurio, un pseudosuquio pariente lejano de los cocodrilos modernos.

facts.statement: Unlike modern crocodiles, aetosaurs like Typothorax were herbivores.
facts.quote: A diferencia de estos, los aetosaurios eran herbívoros.

facts.statement: Typothorax possessed small, leaf-shaped teeth that prevented it from eating meat.
facts.quote: El typothorax y otros aetosaurios poseían dientes pequeños en forma de hoja que no les permitían alimentarse de carne.

facts.statement: Unlike other aetosaurs such as Desmatosuchus, Typothorax lacked large spines on its shoulders.
facts.quote: A diferencia de otros aetosaurios, como el Desmatosuchus, el Typothorax no tiene grandes espinas en los hombros.

facts.statement: Typothorax had two large spines on its neck projecting from the third row of back shields.
facts.quote: Sin embargo, tiene dos espinas grandes en el cuello que se proyectan desde la tercera fila de escudos de la espalda.

facts.statement: Typothorax possessed lateral shields with horns in the posterior region of its back.
facts.quote: Tiene unos escudos laterales con cuernos en la zona posterior de la espalda.

facts.statement: The sides and underside of Typothorax were covered by ornamental shields.
facts.quote: Los laterales y la parte inferior la cubren escudos ornamentados.

facts.statement: T. coccinarum had 10 thoracic and four caudal columns of ventral osteoderms on its underside.
facts.quote: En T. coccinarum hay 10 columnas torácicas y cuatro columnas caudales de osteodermo ventral en la parte inferior.

facts.statement: Unlike all other aetosaurs, Typothorax had pointed osteoderms on the underside of its tail near the cloaca.
facts.quote: A diferencia de todos los demás aetosaurios, Typothorax posee osteodermos puntiagudos en la parte inferior de la cola, cerca de la cloaca.

facts.statement: Like all aetosaurs and many primitive crurotarsians, Typothorax had upright hind legs.
facts.quote: Como todos los aetosaurios y muchos crurotarsianos primitivos, el Typothorax tenía patas traseras erguidas.

facts.statement: Typothorax had reduced forelimbs that extended outward.
facts.quote: Las extremidades anteriores son reducidas y se dirigían hacia fuera en posición extendida.

facts.statement: Researchers believe various features of Typothorax's forelimbs were adaptations for digging.
facts.quote: Varias de las características de las extremidades anteriores se cree que eran adaptaciones para excavar.

facts.statement: Heckert and other scientists concluded that while Typothorax was not specifically adapted for a fossorial lifestyle, it possessed a digging capability that other aetosaurs lacked.
facts.quote: Heckert y otros científicos concluyeron que el Typothorax no estaba adaptado específicamente para un estilo de vida fosorial, pero tenía la capacidad de excavar que otros aetosaurios no tenían.

facts.statement: The upward-facing snout of Typothorax and other aetosaurs suggests they may have searched for food by rooting in the ground.
facts.quote: El hocico hacia arriba del Typothorax y otros aetosaurios sugiere que podían haber buscado comida hurgando en el suelo.

facts.statement: Typothorax was one of the first Triassic vertebrates from western North America to be named, though it has been studied little since then.
facts.quote: El Typothorax fue uno de los primeros vertebrados del Triásico del oeste de Norteamérica a los que se dio nombre, pero se han estudiado poco desde entonces.

facts.statement: Typothorax is closely related to Redondasuchus.
facts.quote: Está estrechamente relacionado con Redondasuchus.

facts.statement: Parker redescribed the holotype of the type species T. coccinarum in 2013.
facts.quote: Parker redescribió el holotipo de la especie tipo de Typothorax, T. coccinarum en 2013.

facts.statement: Parker found the holotype of T. coccinarum too fragmentary to be valid, classifying it as a nomen dubium.
facts.quote: Se constató que estaba demasiado fragmentado y que, por lo tanto, representa un nomen dubium.

facts.statement: To preserve taxonomic stability, Parker suggested requesting a neotype for T. coccinarum from well-preserved specimens with prior references.
facts.quote: No obstante, para preservar la estabilidad taxonómica, Parker sugirió solicitar un neotipo para T. coccinarum a partir de especímenes bien conservados para los que existan referencias anteriores.

facts.statement: The genus Typothorax was named by Cope in 1875.
facts.quote: PBDB name: Typothorax (genus), Cope 1875

facts.statement: Typothorax is classified within the family Stagonolepididae.
facts.quote: Family: Stagonolepididae

facts.statement: Typothorax lived from the Norian to the Rhaetian stages, between 227.3 and 201.4 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Norian to Rhaetian (227.3 to 201.4 million years ago)

facts.statement: The type species of the genus Typothorax is T. coccinarum.
facts.quote: Type species: Typothorax coccinarum

facts.statement: The distinction between Redondasuchus and Typothorax was supported by the description of a new species, R. rineharti, in 2006.
facts.quote: La distinción de Redondasuchus de los Typothorax ha sido apoyada con la descripción de una nueva especie, R. rineharti, en 2006.

facts.statement: Heckert and other scientists argue that Redondasuchus is distinct from Typothorax because its paramedian osteoderms are very flexed, whereas Typothorax's are more gently arched.
facts.quote: Heckert, basándose en nuevo material esquelético, afirma junto a otros científicos que el Redondasuchus es distinto del Typothorax porque tiene osteodermos paramedianos muy flexionados, mientras que Typothorax tiene osteodermos paramedianos arqueados más suavemente.
